indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B5.5.4.1 Know that climate change is one of the most important environmental issues facing the world today
indicator.objective: Identify the impact of deforestation on climate change

skills.description: Define deforestation as the cutting down of trees in a large area.
State the importance of trees (provide shade, food, fresh air, help produce rain).
Explain how deforestation contributes to climate change (fewer trees → less carbon dioxide absorbed → hotter environment).
State effects of deforestation (e.g. loss of habitat, soil erosion, less rain, hotter climate).
Suggest ways to reduce deforestation (plant trees, avoid unnecessary cutting, protect forests).
Explain the importance of planting trees to fight climate change.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Cutting trees has no effect on climate.
Planting one tree will not help.
Deforestation only affects animals, not humans.
Trees do not help produce rain.

options: The cutting down of trees in a large area
hints: It is the opposite of planting trees.
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the cutting down of trees in a large area.
questions.misconception: Deforestation is the planting of trees.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of deforestation?
options: Clearing a large forest to build a road
Planting trees in a school compound
hints: Clearing a forest means cutting down trees.
questions.explanation: Clearing a large forest to build a road is an example of deforestation.

answer: the cutting down of trees in a large area
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the cutting down of trees in a large area.

questions.stem: Which of these is an importance of trees?
hints: Think about sitting under a tree on a hot day.
questions.explanation: Trees provide shade, which helps keep the environment cooler.

questions.stem: How do trees help produce rain?
options: They release water vapour into the air
hints: Water vapour helps form clouds and rain.
questions.explanation: Trees release water vapour into the air through transpiration, which helps form clouds and produce rain.
questions.misconception: Trees do not help produce rain.

questions.explanation: Trees are important because they provide shade, food, fresh air and help produce rain.

questions.stem: Why are trees important for the air we breathe?
options: They take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen
They release carbon dioxide and take in oxygen
questions.explanation: Trees take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which helps keep the air clean for living things.

questions.stem: How does deforestation contribute to climate change?
options: Fewer trees mean less carbon dioxide is absorbed, making the environment hotter
More trees grow and cool the earth
Trees stop the rain from falling
Cutting trees makes the air cleaner
hints: Less trees mean more carbon dioxide in the air.
questions.explanation: Deforestation reduces the number of trees that absorb carbon dioxide, so more carbon dioxide stays in the air and the environment gets hotter.
questions.misconception: Cutting trees has no effect on climate.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Cutting trees has nothing to do with climate change.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, cutting trees does not affect climate
No, cutting trees reduces the number of trees that absorb carbon dioxide, contributing to climate change
No, cutting trees makes the climate cooler
No, cutting trees only affects animals
hints: Less trees mean more carbon dioxide in the air.
questions.explanation: Cutting trees reduces the number of trees that absorb carbon dioxide, which contributes to climate change.
questions.misconception: Cutting trees has no effect on climate.

questions.stem: Explain how deforestation leads to climate change.
answer: cutting down trees reduces the number of trees that absorb carbon dioxide, so more carbon dioxide stays in the air and the earth gets hotter
fewer trees mean less carbon dioxide is absorbed and the environment gets hotter
deforestation increases carbon dioxide in the air, leading to a hotter climate
hints: Less trees mean more carbon dioxide in the air.
questions.explanation: Deforestation reduces the number of trees that absorb carbon dioxide. With fewer trees, more carbon dioxide remains in the air, which traps heat and contributes to climate change.
questions.misconception: Cutting trees has no effect on climate.

questions.stem: Which of these best explains why deforestation makes the environment hotter?
options: Fewer trees means less shade and less carbon dioxide absorption
questions.explanation: Deforestation makes the environment hotter because there are fewer trees to provide shade and absorb carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: What can happen to animals when trees are cut down?
hints: Trees are homes for many animals.
questions.explanation: When trees are cut down, animals lose their homes and habitats.

questions.stem: Which of these is an effect of deforestation?
hints: Without tree roots, soil can wash away.
Trees hold the soil in place.
questions.explanation: Deforestation can lead to soil erosion because tree roots are no longer there to hold the soil in place.
Effects of deforestation include loss of animal habitats, soil erosion, less rain and a hotter climate.

options: It can reduce rainfall because fewer trees release water vapour
It increases rainfall because trees block clouds
It has no effect on rainfall
It makes rain fall only at night
hints: Less trees mean less vapour for rain.
questions.explanation: Deforestation can reduce rainfall because fewer trees release water vapour into the air, which is needed for cloud formation and rain.
questions.misconception: Trees do not help produce rain.

questions.stem: Which of these helps reduce deforestation?
hints: Planting trees is the opposite of cutting them.
questions.explanation: Planting trees helps reduce deforestation by replacing trees that have been cut down.

questions.stem: Give one way to reduce deforestation.
questions.explanation: Ways to reduce deforestation include planting trees, avoiding unnecessary cutting, and protecting forests.

questions.stem: A community wants to reduce deforestation. Which plan is BEST?
options: Plant new trees and protect existing forests
Cut down all trees for farming
hints: Cutting and burning make it worse.
questions.explanation: The best plan is to plant new trees and protect existing forests, which helps reduce deforestation.
questions.misconception: Planting one tree will not help.

questions.stem: In groups, plant a tree seedling in your school compound or a nearby area. Describe the steps you took and explain why planting trees helps fight climate change.

criteria.description: Planted a tree seedling correctly (dug a hole, placed the seedling, covered with soil, watered)
Explained that trees absorb carbon dioxide
Explained that trees help cool the environment and produce oxygen

hints: Dig a hole, place the seedling, cover it with soil, and water it.
Trees absorb carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.
